findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Observed employee use bare hands to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. Discussed proper handwashing procedures. Ensure that a barrier is used to operate faucet handles after washing hands to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands. 

Additionally, be aware of proper gloves use. Be sure to change gloves whenever contamination arises.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The display case that holds baked goods (including TCS foods) were observed with an ambient temperature of 55F. The PIC indicated that the case was recently turned on prior to visit. Discussed switching on the case and allowing the temperature to reach a proper cold holding temperature before adding product. A probed thermometer was placed inside of the unit and it was measured at 44F toward the end of the inspection. Violation corrected on site. Ensure that cold holding temperatures are maintained at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were several mouse droppings observed on the floors throughout the kitchen space. These spaces included in the corner near the walk in freezer and the narrow space behind the dish machine. The facility does have active pest control, however, it is the employees’ responsibility to ensure that the premise is maintained clean and free of insects. Will follow-up on April 17, 2026 to check that droppings are cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: Upon arrival, hot water was’t available to wash hands. The PIC flipped a switch to allow hot water at the sink, however, this caused the circuit breaker to pop, causing the water to shut off. Discussed unplugging pieces of equipment that are not in use for the time being. Hot water became available at a constant flow. Ensure that hot water is available to meet hot water demands. Will follow-up on April 17, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. 
During the last two inspections conducted at The Railyard for the various permitted entities, it has been noted that the dish machine is not properly operating. As this is a shared kitchen, it is imperative that those pieces of equipment being shared are monitored and maintained. Each permitted entity needs to share the responsibility of maintaining this crucial piece of equipment. If the dish machine is not properly operating, dishes are not being sanitized. 
As the kitchen is now closed for the season, SCDPH has decided to start the 2026 operating year with everyone having a clear understanding of what it means to take responsibility for shared space. A spot check with a follow-up will be issued to all permitted entities within the shared space should there be a continued failure to monitor communal goods. 
The area around the dish machine is observed soiled and the dish machine is testing at 0ppm Cl. This correction should occur before the beginning of the 2026 operational year. 



A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).
